Conservation of Medicinal Plants and Traditional Knowledge 
*102. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:†† 
SHRI HARISH RAWAT. 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) the elements of the National Programme for Prom oting Conservation of 
Medicinal Plants and Traditional Knowledge; 
(b) the organizational structure set up to implemen t various objectives of the 
programme and hat manner the finances are being del egated to the participating 
States; and 
(c) the number of States which have identified the sites for the conservation of 
medicinal the details of the medicinal plants. State-wise, and area-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) A project entitled "National Programme on Promo ting Conservation of 
Medicinal Plants and Traditional Knowledge for Enha ncing Health and Livelihood 
Security" has been taken up in  he States, namely K erala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, 
Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, West Bengal, Rajasthan, Man arashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh, with financial support from United Nations  Development Programme 
(UNDP). The project started in May, 2006 with UNDP contribution of US $ 3 
million (approx. Rs. 12 crores), to be completed in  four and half years. The main 
elements of the project include: establishment of a system for rapid threat assessment 
and trade regulation; a network of Medicinal Plant Conservation Areas (MPCAs), 
State level medicinal plant seed centre; method for  sustainable harvest and 
augmentation; home herbal garden; coummunity knowle dge registers and 
mainstreaming traditional medicine into official primary helth programme. 
The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Santosh Bagrodia . 

2    Oral  Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
(b) The Union Ministry of Environment and Forests is th e National Executing 
Agency for the programme and the Foundation for Rev italization of Local Health 
Tradition (FRLHT), Bangalore is the technical coord inating agency. The Forest 
Departments of the concerned States are the designa ted nodal agencies for 
implementation. The funds are released by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to 
the FRLHT for further release to the implementing agencies. The funds so disbursed 
are reimbursed by UNDP to the Government. 
(c) Under the project only four States viz. Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, West Bengal 
and Rajasthan were required to identify sites for c onservation. Of these, three States 
namely Madhya Pradesh, Orissa and Rajasthan have identified sites for conservation 
upto October, 2007. Teams of Taxonomists have been constituted for inventorisation 
of medicinal plants. 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, medicinal plants are very important not only 
for our country but for humanity, as a whole, becau se the kind medicines that are 
produced from them are good even for life threatening diseases. Some very important 
medicines which are made out of them are very impor tant. For example, 
cyclosphorine is used in every transplant case. Wha t I am trying to say is that we 
must try to save them. We must identify them and save them. But the management of 
these particular plants in the Government is handled by many Ministries. I would like 
to know which are the different Ministries who are handling this job because what is 
happening is that these plants are exported to Chin a at a very low rate and, then, in 
China they are re-exporting these at a much higher rate. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: What is the question? 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: What is the Government plann ing so that this 
situation can be reversed? In fact, we should be ab le to process our plants in our 
own country. 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, in the Ministry of Env ironment and 
Forests we are doing the conservation of the medici nal plants. The hon. Member 
wants to know how many Departments or Ministries ar e doing the job for medicinal 
plants. Sir, I would like to inform the hon. Member, through you, that in Government 
of India there is a National Medicinal Plant Board under the Department of AYUSH 
in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. That is the nodal agency for the 
conservation, development, processing and marketing of the medicina. plants. So far as 
research work is concerned, the Ministry of Science and Technology is involved in the 
research and promotion. The DBT, DHT and CSIR are doing this job. In the Ministry 
of Agriculture there are institutions like ICAR, Na tional Horticulture Mission, 
National Board for Horticulture, etc. which are doing cultivation and breeding aspects 
of the medicinal plants. The Ministry of Commerce is involved in the marketing and 
export of the medicinal plants whereas my Ministry,  the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests, is doing conservation and protection a nd also some promotional job 
through some special projects. So far as the questi on that some plants are being 
exported to China and other countries is concerned,  Sir, I would like to inform the 
hon. Member that there is an Act known as Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and under 
that if any flora or fauna is to be sent outside, p ermission will have to be obtained 
from the authority concerned. 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, my second supplementary  is that the 
Ministry has identified under the project only four  States to identify sites for 
conservation. Rajasthan is one of them. They have already identified. I would like to 
know from the hon. Minister what kind of financial, assistance is offered to the State 
for the development of plant and also what is happe ning to the home herbal garden 
schemes amongst various citizen towns because these  plants do not require large 
spaces and this is like dadi's medicine, Sir, if these plants can be developed at home, 
then, a lot of medical problems can be solved at home only. 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions   3 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, we are running a progr amme that is 
called National Programme on Promoting Conservation  of Medicinal Plants in 
traditional knowledge for enhancing health and live lihood security. This is a 
UNDP funded programme and my Ministry is the facili tator and the implementing 
agency is FRLHT. It is a centre of excellence in me dicinal plants. So far as 
Rajasthan is concerned, it is covered under this pr ogramme and necessary funding 
is made through this implementing agency. Regarding  herbal gardens, this is one 
of the components. Under this and through this sche me, funding is being made to 
the persons who desire to have a herbal garden.

Shortcomings in TRAI Act 
*103. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be please d to 
state: 
(a) whether the Telecom Regulatory Authority of lndia (TRAI) Act which came into 
being in 1997 and in which many amendments have already been made, still has many 
shortcomings for which further amendments are required; 
(b) if so. whether the shortcomings have been indentified by Government; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) by when, necessary amendments are proposed to be made in the said Act? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (d) A Statement i s laid on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (c) TRAI Act, 1997 was amended once in Janua ry, 2000 by the Telecom 
Regulator, Authority of India (Amendment) Act. 2000. Subsequently a proposal has 
been received from TRAI for certain amendments to T RAI Act. 1997, to address 
various issues relating mainly to more operational freedom to TRAI and 
administration of broadcasting services. 
(d) The amendments proposed by TRAI in the TRAI Act . 1997 requires inter-
ministerial consultation before finalization of Government's views in this regard. No 
definite time-frame can, therefore, be given for ca rrying out the proposed 
amendment or otherwise. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir. one of the promises  made by the 
UPA Government, when it took office in 2004. was that it would review and strengthen 
the independent regulatory institutions, including telecom. The reason for this was 
obvious. It is clear that some of the regulatory institutions, more specifically, the one 
in telecom sector, have clearly not lived up to exp ectations in both, independence 
and quality. Unfortunately, very little has been do ne in this regard. Therefore, I 
would respectfully submit to the hon. Minister and push him for some specific 
answers. So, my first supplementary is that section 11 of the TRAI Act provides for 
an accord— "The authority shall ensure transparency  while exercising its powers 
in discharging its functions". I would submit that there is very little clarity on it 
really means vis-a-vis the responsibility of the TRAI. So, would the hon. Minister 
think it appropriate that the Act be amended to pro vide clarity on this section and 
to provide a stronger and more vigorous oversight of the Parliament on the TRAI. 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, it is needless to submit before the House that 1 RAI is a 
Body which is constituted under a statute. Section 11 provides how the 
recommendations of the TRAI can be accepted and admitted by the Government as 
soon as it received the recommendations. So far as the recommendations made by 
the TRAI are concerned, most of the recommendations  were accepted by the 
Government. In case any deviation between the Ministry and the TRAI Regulator is 
there, the matter can be remitted to the TRAI by vi rtue of section 11. Such a case 
does not arise. If it arises, then, it will be remi tted back to the TRAI So, I do not 
think that, as such, section 11 needs any further amendment. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir, I would respectfully disagree with the 
Minister, but I hope that this can be further discu ssed. But, let me put a second 
supplementary which 

6    Oral Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
arises from a very interesting episode. Recently, a few telecom operators got together 
and raised the consumer prices almost simultaneously indicating to almost any casual 
observer that there was, perhaps, a case of collusi on. But the Regulator dismissed 
this by-calling it, for the first time, I heard thi s word, 'cooperative pricing'. Sir, is it 
not, again, a case to be made that the TRAI Act sho uld provide for more punitive 
powers to the Regulator to prevent such collusive, and, sort of, abuse of market 
power kind of strategies by the operators? 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, by virtue 6f section 11(3), no d oubt the Regulator; TRAI is 
competent to advise or give recommendations in term s of tariff. Fortunately or 
unfortunately, the recommendations or feelings of the TRAI so far are that it does not 
want to give any tariff since it wanted to stick to  the concept of forbearance. The 
concept of forbearance may, as the hon. Member put it before the House, 'may' lead 
or prompt them to have a cartel within the operator s. This point was well taken by 
me. If it is necessary, I will have consultation with the TRAI, and the matter can be

Question No. 104. 
Grant of carbon credits to domestic companies 
*104. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA : †† 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has set up any national level me chanism to calculate 
and grant carbon credits to domestic companies; 
(b) whether Government have made any estimates of the p otential for domestic 
industry in carbon trade; 
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and 
(d) whether Government propose to hold capacity buildin g programme for the 
private and public industries in carbon trade? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMEN T AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (d) A Stat ement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (d) The Government of India has set up the N ational Clean Development 
Mechanism (CDM) Authority which is the designated N ational Authority for 
according Host Country Approval to eligible project s. Further validation of 
projects, including calculation of Certified Emissi on Reductions.(CERs), is 
undertaken by the Designated Operational Entities ( DOEs). Based on DOE 
recommendations, the Carbon Credits are issued by t he CDM Executive Board 
(EB), by following the stipulated procedure. 
As per National Strategy Study conducted in the yea r 200S, estimates of the 
potential for domestic industry with regard to gene ration of Certified Emission 
Reductions (CERs) are around 417 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide equivalent 
(MtC02eq) by the end of first commitment period of Kyoto Protocol i.e. 2012. 
Sector-wise break-up is as follows—Power generation  —319 MtC02eq, 
Transport—41 MtC02eq, Industries—57 MtC02eq. 
†† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shrimati Prema 
Cariappa. 

8    Oral Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
The Central Government has been actively involved i n Capacity Building of 
private and public sectors. A number of workshops h ave been organized in the past, 
and government officials participate in various sem inars organized by industry 
associations and others. The Government has come ou t with CDM Tool Kits in 
collaboration with Asian Development Bank (ADB), wh ich has been well received 
by all stakeholders. The Government had also initia ted capacity building exercise 
with other multilateral agencies, viz. UNDP and GTZ, including capacity building 
of selected State level agencies. 
SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA: Sir, as per the reply of t he Minister, 
according to the National Strategy Study conducted in the year. 2005, estimates of 
the potential for domestic industry with regard to generation of Certified Emission 
Reductions (CERs) are around 417 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide equivalent by 
the end of first commitment period of Kyoto Protoco l, i.e., 2012. 1 understand that 
the Kyoto Protocol will expire in 2012. What will h appen after that? This is what I 
would like to know from the hon. Minister. 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, the first commitment p eriod of Kyoto 
Protocol will end in 2012. However, discussions are  on further, deeper and longer 
commitments for Annexe I countries for the second c ommencement period post 
2012. 
SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA: Sir, my second supplementa ry is,—it is 
part(d) of my question—will the hon. Minister tell which are the States and State-
level agencies with which the Central Government is  actively involved in capacity 
building of private and public sector? 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, we have done a lot of capacity-building 
programmes. With the help of various organisations like the UNDP-MoEF umbrella 
project on capacity-building of selected State-leve l agencies for small-scale CDM 
projects for Iearning-by-doing-routine, in 13 State s CDM facilitation centres have 
been commissioned. These include Arunachal Pradesh,  Uttaranchal, Tamil Nadu, 
Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, West Bengal, Madhya  Pradesh, Gujarat, Goa, 
Orissa, Jharkhand, Haryana and Bihar. We have also got a GTZ capacity-building 
programme—'Development of Selected Methodologies an d Projects' under CDM, 
technical support to national CDM Authority. Under ADB technical assistance on 
capacity building, the following book was published , "A guide to Tool Kits", for 
implementing small scale CDMs. 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, Carbon trading is a ver y important subject 
in the world today. I would like to know whether th e Government would like to 
start a Carbon trading exchange, which would cover not only Asia and Africa but 
also help international business in a big way. Also , he has said that the Government 
proposes to create a pool of trained offset-aggrega tors, climate-change consultants 
and bankers. What is the price earned by Indian entities per unit of CER? 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, a debate is going on r egarding the issue 
of Carbon-exchange. This is basically the subject matter of the Finance Ministry. 
Universal Service Obligation Fund 
*105. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be please d to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that two private telecom o perators have been found 
making false claims and drawing excess subsidy from  the Universal Service 
Obligation (USO) Fund for providing services in rural areas; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions   9 
(c) the steps taken by Government against them for making wrong subsidy 
claims? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (c) A Statement i s laid on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement  
(a) Errors have been identified in claims submitted by private and State owned 
service providers who have entered into agreements with Universal Service 
Obligation Fund (USOF). However, all such ineligibl e claims are disallowed at the 
time of claim verification stage itself or subseque ntly at the time of physical 
inspection. 
(b) The errors committed, inter-alia, are arithmetical mistakes, claims against 
faulty, disconnected and closed connections and cla ims for connections ineligible 
areas. 
(c) Following steps are taken with reference to ine ligible claims:— 
(i) All such ineligible claims on detection are disallowed. 
(ii) Based upon implementation experience, the method of claim verification is 
continuously improved for ongoing as well as new activities undertaken by USOF. 
SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Sir, I would like to know f rom the hon. 
Minister what efforts are being made by the Government to take telecom revolution 
to the villages in our country. 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, the question relates to the Univ ersal Service Obligation 
Fund under which rural telephony and rural tele-density is being improved. 
Sir, in terms of financial achievements, right from  the year 2002-03, when the 
USO Fund came into existence with a statutory statu s, so far, the funds 
accumulated, which are non-lapsable, amount to Rs. 14,999 crores. Out of these Rs. 
14,999 crores, till date, Rs. 5375 crores have been  released upto 30th September, 
2007 and a further approximately Rs. 5,000 crores have been earmarked for ongoing 
activities. Out of these funds, the major works being carried out by the Ministry are: 
operation and maintenance of village public telephones, that is, Provision of Village 
public telephones have in the villages where accessibility of telephones has not been 
given to the very remote villages installation of r ural community phones and 
installation of rural direct exchange lines and shared infrastructure for mobile services. 
These are the major activities being carried out by  the USO Fund, the Universal 
Service Obligation Fund. 
In terms of physical achievement, other operators w ere permitted to participate 
in the achievement of the goal. So far, the physical achievement that has been made 
under the USO Fund is the replacement of MARR (Multi-Access Radio Relay) with 
VPTs. Since it is a comparatively old technology, Government wanted to replace the 
MARR technology with VPTs on reliable technology. S o far, 1,79,365 VPTs have 
been replaced out of 1,82,766 MARR VPTs. 
In the other provisions, for rural community phones , so far, through BSNL and 
Reliance, we have provided 37,786 rural community phones out of 43409 RCPs. In 
terms of RDEL (Rural Direct Exchange Lines), so far , about 25 lakh RDELs have 
been provided in 1685 Cost Positive SPCAs. So, in t erms of physical achievement 
and financial achievement also, we are going to giv e fullest rural telephony in the 
near future.

other guidelines. 
SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Any further guidelines? 
SHRI A. RAJA: Adequate guidelines and provisions are available with regard to USO 
Fund. I do not think it is necessary.

*107. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Will the Min ister of 
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government had allocated sufficient funds to the State Government of 
Andhra Pradesh for the current year for the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal 
Mission (JNNURM); 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the projects undertaken for this purpose during the  last three years, State-wise 
especially in Andhra Pradesh; and 
(d) the amount allocated and spent under this mission in each State during the current 
year and the progress achieved so far?   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table 
of the Sabha. 
Statement  
(a) and (b) An indicative allocation of Rs. 18903.0 0 lakh has been made for the 
current year 2007-08 for State of Andhra Pradesh un der Urban Infrastructure and 
Governance (UIG) component of JNNURM. As regards Ur ban Infrastructure 
Development Scheme for Small and Medium Towns (UIDS SMT) another 
component of JNNURM an amount of Rs. 5393.00 lakh h as been provided for 
2007-08.

SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, I would like to know from 
the hon. Minister, since there is lot of migration to the towns, people are migrating in 
large numbers to the towns, population in urban are as is increasing drastically year 
after year. So, it is very difficult for local bodi es, town committees to provide 
water, sanitation, housing, power, for that. I woul d like to know whether any study 
has been conducted regarding migration from rural areas to urban areas, necessities in 
urban areas, and fund position with the local bodie s. Is there any proposal with the 
Government of India for extending financial support to the local bodies for acquiring 
land to provide house sites to the poor people who cannot afford to purchase a 
house site in the urban area? 
SHRI AJAY MAKEN: The question is specifically on JNNURM funds for Andhra 
Pradesh. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: My question was wh ether 
sufficient funds are provided to the State of Andhra Pradesh for providing amenities 
for the people in urban areas. I think, it is part of my question. 
SHRI AJAY MAKEN: I would like to tell the hon. Member that the whole concept 
of Urban Renewal Mission is to provide the urban local bodies with sufficient funds 
and simultaneously, to carry out reforms in urban l ocal bodies so that they are 
financially strong enough and viable enough to sustain with the funds which we are 
providing, so that all the projects become sustainable. 
As far as the water supply and other important thin gs, as raised by the hon. 
Member, are concerned, I would like to tell that water supply, sanitation and sewage, 
these are all areas where 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions    13 
we are giving prime importance. He would be glad to know that under UIDSSMT, 60 per 
cent of the total money is given for the water supply, and 17 per cent for the sewage. So, 
water supply and sewage are being given adequate importance. As far as Andhra Pradesh is 
concerned, I would like to tell that in the last two years alone, under UIDSSMT, we have 
been able to give Rs. 235.46 crores, and under UIG we have been able to give Rs. 137.31 
crores on all such projects. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, my question was regarding migration 
from the rural areas to the urban areas. Is there any study done in that regard? While coming 
to my second supplementary question, I leave it to the hon. Minister if he chooses to 
answer my first question, I will be happy; otherwise, I won't mind. Sir, as far as second 
part of my question is concerned, I have the details of the schemes sanctioned for my own 
State, Andhra Pradesh, and I would like to know fro m the hon. Minister about the 
proposals sent by the Government of Andhra Pradesh with regard to Urban infrastructure and 
Governance (UIG) and Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small and Medium 
Towns (UIDSSMT). I would like to know how many projects are sanctioned and how 
many are pending. Is there any time-frame for that? 
SHRI AJAY MAKEN: Sir, I would like to tell the hon. Member that as far as Urban 
Infrastructure and Governance is concerned, in total, 33 projects have been approved. As far as 
projects under appraisal are concerned, only two projects are pending with the Central 
Government for appraisal. As far as projects returned to the State of Andhra Pradesh for 
modification are concerned, in total 38 projects have been send back to them for modification 
because different objections have been raised by the appraisal agencies. As far as UIDSSMT 
projects are concerned, 52 projects are pending because already we have sanctioned and 
released much more amount than what was due for the State of Andhra Pradesh. So, the 
projects, which are pending under the UIDSSMT, are pending because Andhra Pradesh has 
already got the money which is more than its share. 
As far as migration of population to urban areas is concerned, I would like to tell the 
hon. Member that now around 30 per cent of our population lives in the urban areas. It is 
envisaged that by the year 2025, another 10 to 15 per cent of our population will be in 
urban areas. So, all our attention, through JNNURM, is to satisfy the migrated propulation 
as wall as those who are already living in the urban areas.

*113. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be p leased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has initiated any instructio n/guidelines to the 
private and Government hospitals for usage and disp osal of mercury, because the 
minimal risk level for mercury of 0.2 micro gram, but in hospitals the mercury level 
is forty times higher than the normal limit which l eads to neuro-developmental 
disorders in newborns;

FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (d) Improp er handling and 
breakage of instruments containing mercury contaminates the solid waste generated in 
hospitals and can cause environmental pollution.

circulated by the Central Pollution Control Board ( CPCB) to all State Pollution 
Control Boards (SPCBs), Pollution Control Committee s (PCCs) in Union 
Territories and other conterned agencies. The CPCB has also issued instructions to 
all the SPCBs and PCCs that mercury spillages/losse s in health care facilities need

manufacturers, and measures are taken to ensure tha t the spilled mercury does not 
become part of the bio-medical or other solid waste  generated from the healthcare 
facilities. Any waste containing equal to or greate r than 50 ppm or mercury is 
categorized as hazardous waste as per the Hazardous  Wastes (Management & 
Handling) Rules, 2003 and healthcare facilities are  required to dispose of such 
wastes in accordance with the said Rules. The SPCBs / PCCs have also been 
requested to bring this aspect/requirement to the notice of the healthcare facilities and 
ensure incorporation of appropriate conditions in the authorizations granted by them 
under the Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, 1998.

notice of the Government.

FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) Discharges of  effluent from the

(c) The efforts taken by the Government for control of industrial pollution

Undertakings/ State Electricity Utilities, increasing private investments and

utilities, enlarges the scope of captive power plants and has emphasized the 
development of hydro power.

feasible hydro potential, debt financing of longer tenure.

holiday regime for a period often years. The thresh old limit to obtain the 
mega power status is 1000 MW for thermal and 500 MW  for hydro

† 423.       DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI:    
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 'Thorium' is likely to be  available in massive quantity 
in the country; 
(b) if so, whether it is possible to utilize it for generating electricity in the Atomic 
Sector: 
(c) if so, the facts thereof; and 
(d) the present status regarding the availability of th e said storages of 'Thorium' 
in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFIC E (SHRI 
PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) Yes, Sir. 
(c) While Thorium by itself cannot serve as a fuel for generating power in a 
nuclear reactor, it can be converted to Uranium-233 which is a man made fuel when 
suitably irradiated in a nuclear reactor. 
India has formulated a three stage nuclear power pr ogramme to optimally use its 
modest uranium and vast thorium resources to fulfil  the increasing energy 
requirements of the country. Large scale thorium ut ilization is contemplated in the 
third stage of this programme, where Uranium-233 br ed in fast breeder reactors of 
the second stage, will be used together with thoriu m. The Government has taken a 
number of steps to develop appropriate technologies for the utilization of thorium. A 
few of the major steps are: 
(1) Setting up the research reactor Kamini at Kalpakkam using Uranium-233 fuel 
obtained from irradiated thorium. The reactor has been operating since 1997. 
The fuel for the reactor is bred, reprocessed and fabricated indigenously. 
(2) Irradiation of thorium fuel bundles in research rea ctor at Trombay and in 
Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs). 
(3) Design and development of Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (AHWR) using 
thorium based fuel. Pre-licensing safety review of AHWR has been 
completed by Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB). 
(4) India has developed technologies to reprocess irradiated thorium fuel and in 
fabricating Uranium-233 based fuel. 
(d) Thorium in India is mainly recovered from a naturally occurring mineral-monazite. 
Monazite is produced as a co-product alongwith ilmenite, zircon, rutile, etc. A quantum 
of Thorium in the form of thorium concentrate is pr oduced as a by-product of rare 
earth compounds which are recovered from monazite. 30,000 (thirty thousand) tonnes 
of such thorium concentrate is stored in silos for future use.

Rules regarding Electromagnetic Radiation 
1434.      SHRI MOTILAL VORA: 
SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION  
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Electromagnetic Radiation  (EMR) always continue 
from mobile phone towers; 
(b) if so, the effects of EMR on human body; 
(c) the rules regarding setting up of mobile phone towers; 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(e) the time by when rules will be framed in this direction; and 
(0 whether Government will arrange for strict monitoring till the rules are framed 
in this regard?   . 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICAT IONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a)  to (f) 
Yes, Sir. The electromagnetic radiations are always  present from any antenna 
emitting radio signals, whether it is a mobile phon e tower or a broadcast tower etc. 
The level of electromagnetic radiations within safe ty limits is harmless. The latest 
Fact Sheet of World Health Organisation (WHO) (No. 304 of May, 2006) states that 
from all evidence accumulation so far, no adverse s hort or long-term health effects 
have been shown to occur from the RF signals produc ed by base station. Since 
wireless networks produce generally lower RF signals than base stations, no adverse 
health effects are expected exposure to them. Further, a Committee was setup under 
the Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), as per the orders 
of Hon'ble High Court, Mumbai, to study the effects  of radiations from mobile 
phone towers and related aspects. The Committee had  studied the effects and 
concluded that overall there is not enough evidence to show direct health hazards of 
RF exposures from mobile base stations.

Melting of Gomukh Glacier 
 447. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Gomukh glacier, the origin of Gangotri (river Ganges) is melting 
and slowly vanishing; 
(b) if so, details thereof and reasons therefor; 
(c) its impact on the availability of water during next two decades; and 
(d) the steps being taken to save and restore the existence of Gomukh glacier? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) The studies carried out by Department of 
Science and Technology on Gangotri Glacier have revealed that the Glacier was receding at the 
rate of 17.15 m/year during 1971-2004 period. Another study estimated a retreat of 12.10 m 
during the year 2004-05. Compilations of the data on secular movement of glaciers have revealed 
that the majority of the glaciers of the Himalayan region are passing through a phase of recession, 
which is a worldwide phenomenon. The causative factors for this variable retreat may be 
subnormal snowfall, higher temperature during summer, less severe winter or a combination of 
all of them. It could also be attributed to the phenomenon of rise in temperature, global warming, 
to some extent. 
(c) The Government has not undertaken any study to correlate the river discharge, water 
level changes in sea and ocean and the recession of the glaciers. In addition to the glaciers, 
seasonal snow cover, groundwater and rainfall contribute to the river discharge. Due to enhanced 
melting of ice, consequent upon faster recession, the runoff of the Himalayan rivers may 
increase marginally. 
(d) The recession of glaciers cannot be prevented on a large scale in view of the nature of 
Indian Himalayan Glaciers being debris covered, the economic feasibility, the scale of operation 
and the likelihood of pollution. As the prime responsibility of reducing emissions that enhance 
global warming lies with the developed countries, the Government of India has been pressing in 
international negotiations that these countries should take deeper emission reduction commitments 
and for a longer period.

National policy for global warming  
465. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR Will the PRIME MINIS TER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulate a new national po licy for addressing the 
issue of global warming; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, by when that is likely to be done? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMEN T AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) The N ational 
Environment Policy 2006 of Ministry of Environment & Forests inter alia 
addresses the issue of global warming. The followin g comprise essential elements 
of India's response to climate change: 
(1) Adherence to the principle of common but differenti ated responsibilities 
and respective capabilities of different countries in respect of both 
mitigation of green house gases (GHGs), an adaptation measures. 
(2) Reliance on multilateral approaches, as opposed to bilateral or plurilateral or 
unilateral measures. 
(3) Equal per-capita entitlements of global environmental resources to all 
countries. 
(4) Over-riding priority of the right to development. 
(5) Identify key vulnerabilities of India to climate change, in particular impacts 
on water resources, forests coastal areas, agricultre, and health. 
(6) Assess the need for adaptation to future climate ch ange, and the scope for 
incorporating these in relevant programmes, including watershed management, 
coastal zone planning and regulation; forestry mana gement, agricultural 
technologies and practices, and health programmes. 
(7) Encourage Indian Industry to participate in the Cle an Development 
Mechanism (CDM) through capacity building for ident ifying and 
preparing CDM projects, including in the financial sector 
(8) Participate in voluntary partnerships with other co untries both developed 
and developing, to address the challanges of sustai nable development and 
climate change, consistent with the provisions of t he UN Framework 
Convention on Climate Change. 
Further, the Government has also set up "Expert Committee on Impacts of Climate 
Change" in May 2007 to study the impacts of anthropogenic climate change on India 
and to identify the measures that we may have to ta ke in the future in relation to 
addressing vulnerability to anthropogenic climate change impacts. 
Acoordination committee chaired by Hon'ble Prime Mi nister called "Prime 
Minister's Council on Climate Change to coordinate national action for assessment, 
adaptation and mitigation of climate change" was constituted on 6th June 2007. The 
focus of the Committee would be to: 
I. Evolve a coordinated response to issues relating to climate change at the 
national level; 
II. Provide oversight for formulation of action plans in the area of assessment, 
adaptation and mitigation of climate change; 
III.  Periodically monitor key policy decisons.

Statement  
Details regarding scheme for giving Legal/Financial Assistance to women 
deserted by theirOverseas Indian Spouses  
I. Objective: 
The objective of the scheme is to provide some fina ncial assistance to needy 
women in distress who have been deserted by their O verseas Indian spouses for 
obtaining counseling and legal services. The term " Overseas Indian" would include 
NRIs and foreign citizens of Indian origin. The cou nseling and legal services would 
be provided through credible Indian Women's Organiz ations/Indian Community 
Associations and NGOs identified for providing such  services and empanelled with 
the Indian Missions in the USA, the UK, Canada, Aus tralia, New Zealand and the 
Gulf. The scheme is a welfare measure to support wo men of Indian origin in 
distress, through the mobilization of the local Ind ian community in the endeavour 
and with some financial assistance from the Governm ent. 
II. Scope of and eligibility for the Scheme: 
The scheme would be available to the women who have  been deserted by their 
overseas Indian spouses or are facing divorce proce edings in a foreign country 
subject to the following conditions:— 

72    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
(i) The woman is an Indian passport holder. 
(ii) The marriage of the woman has been solemnized in India. 
(iii) The woman is deserted in India or after reach ing abroad within five years 
of the marriage. 
(iv) Divorce proceedings are initiated within five years of the marriage by her 
overseas Indian spouse. 
(v) An ex-parte divorce has been obtained by the overseas Indian spouse within 
ten years of the marriage and a case for maintenanc e and alimony is to be 
filed. 
(vi) The scheme would not be available to a woman f acing criminal charges or 
having a criminal case decided against her. 
(vii) The domicile of the woman seeking relief under the scheme is not relevant for 
allowing the benefit. The woman may be domiciled in  the country of her 
overseas Indian spouse or in India at the time of making the application. 
(viii) Preference may be given to applicants on the basis of financial needs. 
(ix) Assistance will be limited to meeting initial cost and incidental charges for 
documentation and filing of the case by the Indian women's 
organization/NGO on the woman's behalf. 
(x) The assistance will be limited to US $ 1000 per case and will be released to 
the Indian community organizations/NGO concerned to  enable it to take 
steps to assist the woman in documentation and prep aratory work for filing 
the case. 
(xi) The women's organization/NGO will make efforts  to enlist community 
advocates, preferably women advocates, to extend fu rther legal 
assistance/appearance in court etc. on a pro-bono basis. 
Pattern of Assistance 
Under the scheme Indian Missions in the countries c oncerned would empanel 
credible Indian Women's Organizations/Indian Community Associations/NGOs and 
their member advocates, preferably women, to provid e legal aid to the victims in 
distress and whose names have been approved by the Ministry of Overseas Indian 
Affairs. The applications for providing legal aid r eceived by the Missions would by 
examined by an officer designated by the Head of th e Mission on case-to-case basis 
and approved by Head of Mission/Deputy Chief of the Mission. 
The applications received in the Ministry of Overse as Indian Affairs will be 
examined by an internal committee consisting of a legal advisor and an officer of the 
rank of Director/Deputy Secretary and approved by S ecretary. Thereafter, the 
Ministry will recommend the case to Mission concern ed to provide legal aid 
support. The applicant would also be informed to ap proach the Mission concerned 
in this regard.

(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. A research project R-64 entitled "Establishment of System for 
Identification and Rectification of Accident Black Spots" was undertaken by this 
Ministry in the year 1995. 18 selected sections of 100m each on 15NHs were

Based on accident analysis, the following conclusio ns have been drawn with 
regards to road accidents, their causes, occurrence s, causalities and vehicle 
improvement. 
(i) Maximum number of accidents, especially fatal a ccidents are found to 
occur on straight stretches due to high speed. 
(ii) Four arm junctions were found to be most vulne rable mainly due to 
insufficient site distance, lack of traffic guidance, absence of road markings 
and poor road geometries. 
(iii) Head on collisions are found to be maximum du e to high speed and bad 
overtaking practice. 
(iv) Pedestrians are most vulnerable victims due to  insufficient pedestrian 
facilities and poor knowledge of about traffic rule s. Pedestrians are ranked 
second in making errors and one of the main causes of accidents.

Unauthorised occupation of plots for slum dwellers  
525. SHRI VARINDER SINGH BAJWA: Will the Minister o f URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of plots allotted by MCD and DDA for the  rehabilitation of slum 
dwellers which have unauthorisedly been grabbed by unauthorised persons; 
(b) if so, whether an inquiry has been made in the matt er, particularly with 
reference to an involvement of MCD, DDA and other a dministrative staff of Delhi 
Administration; and 
(c) if so, the outcome of the inquiry and the action taken/proposed to be taken in 
the matter? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) to (c) Central B ureau of 
Investigation (CBI) has reported that it has regist ered two cases relating to alleged 
scam in the allotment of resettlement plots to slum  dwellers by MCD and DDA. In 
one case, charge-sheet has been filed on 5.11.2007 against four DDA officials, two ex-
DDA officials, one official of Delhi Legislative Assembly and one private person. In 
the second case the matter is at investigation stage. 
Procedure for selection for Arjuna Awards  
526. SHRI JAI PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the Minister o f YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the procedure for recommendation/nomination of candidates eligible for the Arjuna 
Awards; 
(b) the procedure followed after the nominations/recommendations have been made 
to select awardees; 
(c) the reason for games like tennis and carom, not being enlisted in drawing 
awardees; and 
(d)the steps taken to make the selection process mo re encompassing of other 
sports and also more transparent in its working? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) The eligibility criteria for th e Arjuna Awards includes 
consistently good performance for the previous thre e years at international level 
coupled with leadership and sportspersonship qualities. The award is considered in 
both Olympic and Non-Olympic disciplines, including  indigenous games and 
sports for the physically challenged. Nominations f or the award are invited from 
recognized National Sports Federations, the Indian Olympic Association, State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations and Sports Control/Promotion Boards 
of various Government organizations such as Police, Army etc. 
(b) The nominations received are duly scrutinized and e ligible nominations are 
placed before an independent selection committee co nsisting of eminent 
sportspersons, including Olympians and past Arjuna Awardees, Government 
representatives and sports administrators. The Selection Committee determines its own 
work procedure and the selection is made by consens us failing which by a majority 
decision. 
(c) and (d) While all disciplines including Tennis and Carom are considered for the 
award, the Selection Committee selects the awardees on the basis of their performance 
at major international events. Since ordinarily not more than 15 awards are given in a 
particular year, it is not possible to cover all sports disciplines every year. In the past, 
several Tennis players have been conferred Arjuna Awards such as S/Shri Ramnathan 
Krishnan, Jaideep Mukherjee, Vijay Amritraj, Ramesh

Krishnan, Anand Amritraj, Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhup ati, Akhtar Ali, Ms. Sania 
Mirza, etc. Similarly, in Carom, Sh. Anthony Maria Irudayam was conferred the 
Arjuna Award.

108    Written Answers to  {RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
Employment against sports quota  
528. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is fact that Subhash Dixit who captained  Indian team to win below 
fifteen World Cup 2000, jumped to death from 6th floor of a building in Kanpur on 9th 
June, 2007 due to poverty and unemployment; 
(b) if so, the reasons he was not given any scholarship or employment against sports 
quota; and 
(c) the steps Government and BCCI propose to take for welfare of 
sportspersons/cricketers? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) to (c) The Ministry has no inde pendent information in this 
regard. BCCI have informed the Ministry that they came to know through media reports 
that Shri Subash Dixit, who was Captain of India Under-15 team for the World Cup-2000, 
had committed suicide by jumping from the 6th floor of a building in Kanpur. This was 
confirmed to BCCI by the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association, Kanpur. BCCI have also 
informed the Ministry that it has a scheme for reti red test and first class cricketers to 
whom monthly gratis is given depending on the number of first class matches a player had 
played. Shri Subash Dixit did not qualify for the benevolent funds scheme.

529. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are not encouraging other sports compared to cricket in the 
country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
(c) the present position thereof; 
(d) the amount allocated and spent under each category of sports during the last three 
years in the country, State-wise; and 
(e) the steps Government are taking to encourage each and every sport in the country 
within a specific time-frame to achieve gold medals in world level competitions? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) to (d) The Ministry of Youth Af fairs and Sports have been 
encouraging all sports disciplines in the country by giving financial assistance to recognized 
National Sports Federations. BCCI which is promoting the sports of Cricket however has 
never applied for financial assistance under the Scheme of the Ministry. Under the Scheme, 
the Ministry is providing financial assistance for participation in International 
Tournaments abroad, organizing International Tourna ments in India, National 
Championships in India, Coaching Camps, engagement of foreign coaches, procurement 
of equipments etc. The financial assistance provide d to various recognized National 
Sports Federations during the last 3 years is given in the Statement (See below), which 
excludes expenditure incurred towards National Coaching Camps and the engagement 
of foreign coaches, which is implemented through the Sports Authority of India. 
(e) To encourage various sports and games in the co untry, financial assistance is 
given to promising sportspersons for training and training-cum-competitions in India: 
and abroad,

That we have recaptured Nandigram by force. Sir, ou r people have gone back to 
Nandigram. Our people, who are the legitimate owner s of their houses, have gone 
back to their houses. Our people, who till those la nds, have gone back to their own 
lands. The children have gone back to their own hom es. And the children, who were 
denied schooling are now restarting their life after one year. Is it a crime for people to 
go back to their homes? Is it a crime for farmers t o go back to till their lands? If they 
are charging us that we have done this through force, I am saying that we have done 
this by resisting the force, not. by employing force; the force was employed from the 
other side. We have resisted that and gone back to our homes. And for 11 months, 
when they were deprived of their homes, when they w ere thrown out as refugees

petroleum investment region. Yes, there was a propo sal there for a chemical hub.

acquired, but, no formal land acquisition notice was ever issued. There was a notice

happened in Nandigram is actually a direct political challenge to destabilise an elected 
Government there, and, that is precisely the logical conclusion that they all want ftflead 
up to seeking imposing President's Rule there. The destablisation of an elected Government—
if this is permitted by the use of extremist forces and Maoist violence—is something that is 
not in the interest of India; forget West Bengal, forget CPI (M). We are playing with fire. If you 
are stoking them and actually patronizing and supporting them in order to settle Petty political 
scores here and there, you are actually playing with the future of the entire country. So, 
Nandigram is an abject lesson for -.»!! of us. All this evidence that I have given shows how 
the Maoists penetrated, how they ha - gone into each of those villages, and, how they 
themselves mocked at the Trinamool

declaration of an armed action against an Indian State. If this is ignored, if that is not

Therefore, with the responsibility that is required  of all of us, we will have to take 
up this issue in the larger context. People who had  actually been driven out of their 
homes have gone back to their homes, as I said, not  by using force but by resisting.

can only ignore at our peril and that larger issue must be kept in mind. Do not reduce 
it only to settle petty political scores. Keep the interest of India in mind. 
This is the appeal that we have to make. I want to asure this august House that as 
far as CPI (M) is concerned, with the fullest confi dence and commitment to the 
democracy that we have shown all these years and wh ich we will continue to show, 
we do not want this process to be undermined. These  forces must be put to check, 
and, that is my sincere appeal. Thank you.

SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Now I'm speaking in Bengali again. Sir, I want to conclude 
with a couplet written by Rabindranath Tagore. Brin daji, you have been singing this 
song for long but might have forgotten now. The song follows like this: 
If you create obstacles, the struggle will ensue and we may have to court death. 
If you block the road, you have to clear the way. 
You want to become rich with the wealth accumulated by looting. 
You will fall on the dusty road just in a minute. 
If you want to shake it, you will also be shaken. 

172   Short Duration [RAJYA SABHA] Discussion  
[SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA] 
If you create obstacles, the struggle will ensue and we may have to court death. 
You have to accept the truth. And please tell the Chief Minister who says, "An eye 
for an eye", that this is not the way. If you want to win over the people, you should 
work on other ways, but not this way. And please al so arrange for their 
rehabilitation. Thank you, Sir. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, we have been discussing since noon 
time about the issue of Special Economic Zones, spe cially Nandigram, and 
consequential violence in that area. Sir, there are two distinct things—one is Special 
Economic Zones and the other part is violence in Na ndigram. Sir, this is an 
unfortunate incident in Nandigram and going by the newspaper reports and going by 
the speeches, I feel that one should express sympat hy to the victims. The 
Government should.take all the steps for rehabilita tion and extending financial 
assistance for all the victims and we should see that normalcy is restored at the earliest. 
Sir, main cause for all these incidents and events,  which are avoidable, is Special 
Economic Zones. The Government of India, as of now, have sanctioned 375 Special 
Economic Zones. Sir, the very purpose is defeated. Sir, going by the trends in the 
country, going by the resistance from land owners, small and marginal farmers, it is 
going to end up as a displaced development and as m isplaced priority. I feel that in 
the name of SEZ, many people, who are close to ruli ng dispensations in various 
States, are floating all the economic zones. We are  aware of the concessions given 
to these Special Economic Zones, specially tax exemptions, duty free import, domestic 
procurement of goods for development, hundred per c ent income tax exemption, 
exemption from minimum alternate tax, exemption from Central sales tax, service tax, 
single window clearance for all these economic zone s etc. For whose benefits, they 
are floating these Special Economic Zones. The Government should have a thorough 
review of these economic zones. In my own State, An dhra Pradesh, 70 Special 
Economic Zones have been cleared. Sir, 25,000 acres of land is going to be acquired, 
and, most of them are already floated there in the State. And, Sir, people who are very 
close to the Ruling Party are floating these Special Economic Zones. Sir, information 
technology companies are also acquiring lands in th e name of Special Economic 
Zones. The concessions are given to the entrepreneurs, and, more than fifty per cent 
concession is availed for real estate purposes. Why  should the Government of India 
or the respective State Government act as middlemen  in acquiring the lands? Sir, 
literally, they have become real estate brokers. 
Sir, now, the land has become very precious, and, in the name of SEZ, people are 
grabbing the agriculture lands. Sir, already, when the cultivable land is shrinking in 
the country and the agricultural production is also  coming down, we are encouraging 
Special Economic Zones in the agricultural fields. Sir, a day will come when instead of 
earmarking Special Economic Zones, we will have to earmark certain land for special 
agricultural fields. Sir, we can call the present SEZs as 'special encroachment zones' 
into the agriculture fields and thereby becoming special exploitation zones. They are 
literally exploiting the fields. 
Sir, the concept of SEZ has to be throughly reviewed. There should be an evaluation. 
Sir, I am having the data with me. Due to paucity of time, I cannot give all the details.

above these things. Sir, the first aspect which I w ish to draw the attention of this 
august House to is the debates when our Constitutio n was being formulated. When 
our Constitution was being formulated in the Consti tuent Assembly, there was a 
debate at some length as to how and how much and what to give to the States in terms 
of Constitutional power. We, ultimately, ended up with the First List of the Constitution 
which is extremely large and very voluminous. The t erritory and the area covered by 
the First List of the Seventh Schedule is, in proportion, much larger than the State List 
or the Concurrent List. That is why from being a fully federal Constitution, we are called 
a quasi-federal Constitution. But, even in that debate— because our founders were 
concerned about the possible break-up of this natio n, about the fissiparous 
tendencies which beset the nation at that time in the context of partition—there was a 
very strong move to say that law and order is somet hing which we must give to the 
States; law and order is something which must be given in the widest possible meaning 
and amplitude to the States because we cannot have the beginning of federalism 
unless we gave law and order, not only as a word, but in spirit and in an enlarged zone 
also to the States. And, that is why, in the

Second List for the States, the first entry is law and order. Even in certain aspects, 
of what the Supreme Court has called the three concentric circles—the narrower circle 
is law and order, the slightly larger circle is pub lic order and the largest circle, is the 
security of the State—the security of the State, th e largest concentric circle, may be 
given and has been given to the Centre. But, the entirety of law and order, and in that 
connected sense, large parts of public order were d eliberately, after much debate, 
much comments by the framers, given to the States. There is a reason for it. And, it is 
for that reason, every State Government—1 don't mean this only for West Bengal, but

THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): There are a number of speakers. 
Hereafter each hon. Member will take five minutes or maximum seven minutes and not more 
than that. 
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY (Karnataka): Up to what time will we sit? 
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): That is why I said that each hon. 
Member would take five minutes or maximum seven minutes. 
DR. BARUN MUKHERJEE (West Bengal): Sir, thank you very much for the 
opportunity given to me. At the same time, there is a stricture that we should restrict our time. 
Sir, all of us know that the problem in Nandigram started with the proposal of SEZ. At 
the outset, I should say, on behalf of my party, the All India Forward Block, that we are 
opposed to this SEZ, as we think that it is the biggest land grab move during the recent times in 
the name of promoting exports, in the name of industrialisation. All this is being done to favour 
a few corporate houses, and some foreign houses, at the cost of millions of poor farmers. It will 
not only affect our food security, but it will also affect the livelihood of millions of poor farmers. So, 
we are firmly against this SEZ policy. And, as it has been noticed, irrespective of political 
affiliations, there has been resistance to SEZs in many other States of the country because the 
poor farmers have felt a pinch that if the farmland is lost, then, everything is lost. So, in spite of our 
representation to the Central Government, unfortunately, this has been rejected and all these 
things are going on. And we also find that the Government of India is merrily giving more and 
more approvals to SEZs; it is apprehended that it may touch tlie figure of thousand within a 
couple of months. So, we are basically opposed to SEZs. The same thing happened when a 
proposal came for establishing an SEZ at Nandigram. Naturally, there was a hue and cry over it. 
We are of the opinion that before the announcement of the SEZ, perhaps, proper homework was 
not done. I can even say, without mentioning the name of anybody, a top-ranking leader of the 
State, during out internal meeting, admitted that they did find afterwards that this acquisition 
would not only cover the farmlands, but also temples, mosques and graveyards. These are all 
being included there. So, there was a panic amongst people. But, unfortunately, this was made 
a political issue and, very quickly, some committee, in the name of Bhumi Uchhed Pratirodh

Sir, I fully endorse Shri Madani's stand—whenever we speak against the Communist 
Party, they resort to Islamic extremism. On the nat ional and international arena, they 
always pose to be the saviours of Islam. But if even a word is spoken about Communist 
Party, then Islamic extremism and mine: ity extremism come in. This is happening here 
also, and that is why, I wished to respond to comrade Yechury's remarks. We did not expect

are treated badly anywhere in India the Communists have been the first to react, be it 
Gujarat or anywhere else. But when it came in West Bengal, the words Shri Yechury used

extremism'. But whenever anything happens anywhere in the world in Muslim-dominated

because when Mr. Madani expressed his views, he expressed mine too. 
Coming back to Nandigram, I had a chance to go to Nandigram after the March incident. 
I would not repeat the things said by Sushmaji and others here; the situation there is 
pathetic. Whatever happens, whether it is laying of road or displacement due to anything else, 
90 per cent of the affected people are Muslims. Nobody is talking about that, everybody is 
talking about farmers and others. Of course, Nandigram is a beautiful place. We could go 
there only on the scooter; the first thing we saw was a beautiful pond and fertile land. It is 
definitely not fit to be made a chemical hub; that is for sure. In Kerala, we adore Shri 
Buddhadeb Bhattacharya, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, as he is a progressive Chief 
Minister. He readily agreed to scrapping this deal but still this problem is going on. We, in 
Kerala, feel that it is not because of SEZs; it is only because of the fact that the nazist 
Communist Party took a decision that if somebody goes against their party, then they 
would take it personally. The Police is not there; their cadres are coming out. This has 
become a prestige issue for them. Otherwise, Nandigram is represented by the CPI; it is not a 
CPM hold. Still, CPM is taking their cadres, without taking Police protection; it is taking it as

Kerala too, in Kannur; Kannur is also a CPM belt. So, we in Kerala fear that this Nandigram

condemn this sort of attitude towards people, especially the majority Muslims. Thank 
you, Sir, for giving me this opportunity.

SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI: Mr. Deputy Chairman, Si r, of the little time 
that is given to me, I want to use half-a-minute for the guillotine that has been applied 
to 'Others' speakers in this House. According to my  information, there were 47 
Members in this House who all in the category of' O thers'. The B.J.P, has 48 
Members and I found the B.J.P, using, at least, one-and-a-half hour and to allot only 
28 minutes to the 'Others' speakers, I think, is pa tently unfair. The Party members 
get time to make sher-o-shayari...  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Mr. Joshi, just to tell you, t he time taken by the 
speakers from 'Others' category so far has far exce eded than the time taken by the 
speakers from all the parties on this debate. The allocated time is 28 minutes, but the 
time taken has exceeded all other parties. That is for your information. 
SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI: That is your generosity . We should get that 
as matter of right. 
Sir, I have the largest possible experience in this  House of farmers' movements. I 
have been active in the anti-SEZ movements not only  in Maharashtra but also in 
Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Haryana also. I have seen so many farmers being killed, 
so much blood flowing that I have no trears left fo r shedding and I can't get into 
anything like poetry or shayari while speaking about the fanners' agitation. I look at it 
in a very prosaic and logical way. I was hoping to find some solutions to some of the 
problems that I was facing in the debate that has now lasted for six hours. There were 
accusations, there were counter-accusations, and there was even a hilarious claim that 
the NGOs, the RSS and the Muslim fundamentalists ha d come under the banner of 
Maoists for attacking the CPI(M) Government, and th en there was also a defence 
from the Treasury Benches of the Maoists raising ho w great Mao was. I think the 
Congress Party will accept that. But I did not get any reply to the questions that I was 
facing. 
Sir, the questions very briefly are as follows: 
One, why was the Nandigram area of Midnapore Distri ct of all the places chosen 
for this particular SEZ? Because it is a lush green area, a very fertile agriculture area 
and the only advantage that it has is that it is closer to some of the water sources which 
was actually used for throwing away the bodies on 1 4th March and again on 16th 
November. But that could have also been useful for taking away the effluents from the 
chemical industry. But apart from that, there is no reason why that region should have 
been chosen. 
I come from Maharashtra and in Maharashtra we have found out a way. The 
principle that we accepted is that those farmers wh o want to continue doing 
agriculture, their land can't be taken away by anybody, and those farmers who do not 
want to continue with agriculture, they have the fu ll right to dispose of their land to 
anybody they like, at whatever price they like and whenever they like. Once this 
principle is accepted, we were able to formulate bodies where the farmers themselves 
undertook the development of the Special Economic Z ones and therefore there has 
not been any kind of conflagration that we are seeing in Nandigram. 
Then, somebody, mentioned that 90 per cent of the p eople who were dead and 
injured were Muslims. Why has that happened? There should be some kind of an 
explanation for that

What was the great high about the idea 'recapture'? Were the people driven out? Why 
did they go out? What about the high about recapture? 
The last question is: Why is it that the ruling par ty in Bengal is using the kind of 
brazenness that was used after Tiananmen Square operation by the Chinese rulers? 
Normally, the Communists do not do that. They very politely try to understand the 
point of view of the other people and try to find a solution. Why is it that they are going 
it? Mr. A.B. Bardhan, with whom I had a talk he is the General Secretary of the CPI 
said that this was the arrogance of power. I don't know if this is the arrogance of 
power or they are in the flush of the recent victor y in Bengal. But this is something 
that I did not expect from them. 
Sir, I also visited Nandigram twice and I took the occasion to go out and talk to the 
people and farmers who were there. The facts that cannot be denied very briefly are as 
follows: On 14th March, two facts were established. The police forces in West Bengal 
have been largely infiltrated and that there has been a deliberate effort to push the party 
cadres into the police force officially. Secondly, there has been a large degree of 
indoctrination of the police forces which is also o f course understandable as this has 
happened in every communist country. Then on 14th M arch again, it was said that 
eight people were killed in the police firing because the bullets were known to be the 
police bullets and six people were killed by the bullets that did not belong to the police. 
Everybody admitted that many people who were using even private firearms and 
wearing uniforms were actually CPI(M) cadre people. It was established later on in the 
CBI inquiry that they were CPI(M) fellows who carri ed on as police people. On 16th 
November, a different thing happened. Now, they were not the private CPI(M) people 
masquerading as police forces. They were ordinary p eople who were looking like 
farmers. They called themselves 'red army' and in a  very military-like operation 
marched over to Nandigram. They put the hostages of  the anti-acquisition people in 
the front, in between, there were the people, CPI(M ) cadres, who were driven out, 
who were supposed to take over and resettle in the villages and the 'red army' was 
firing from behind both of them. The people in the villages did not reply because they 
not want to kill their own brothers. These are the facts which have been established. 
The number of people killed in the months of March was said to be only 14. In fact, 
from the local enquiries, I found that, at least, 200 people were missing and they were 
presumed to be dead. There are witnesses who say th at the dead bodies were 
carried in truckloads and put into the river. Simil arly, the number of people dead in the 
month November and missing as of today, is 400. Sir , I tried to enquire from the 
farmers what lies behind all this. Sir, the simple story, I will try to explain in the way 
Sherlock Holmes explains at the end of the novel, the mystery of the whole Nandigram 
affair. The brazenness of the ruling party comes from the fact that behind Nandigram lies 
a very serious skeletons in their cupboards and they are very keen to hide them. What 
is the skeleton? The skeleton is this. The Communis t Party and the Left front people 
always brage about their land reform programme. The fact is that the land reforms have 
happened in Midnapore and this is the area where ma ximum land reforms have 
happened. Therefore, the Communist Party thought that this is an area where all the 
people who are land-owners are now are the benefici aries of the land reforms 
programme and there would not be any resistance. But, in fact, in the operation of the 
land reforms programme, something very funny happen ed. There was a share-
cropping kind of land reform, to which Shri Priyara njan Dasmunsi referred to and 
there were also direct transfer of the land to the original landless people. The funny 
thing that happened was that the documents relating  to land records, either the 
possession or for the share-cropping, were not transferred to the poeple who received 
the land rights or who received the land. All the d ocuments are in party office.

Message from 22 NOV. 2007 Lok Sabha  205 
MESSAGE FROM LOK SABHA  
The All-india Institute of Medical Sciences And The Post-graduate Institute 
of Medical Education And Research (Amendment) Bill, 2007 
SECRETARY-GENERAL: Sir, I have to report to the House the following message 
received from Lok Sabha, signed by the Secretary-General of Lok Sabha:— 
"In accordance with the provisions of rule 96 of th e Rules of Procedure and 
Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, I am directed to enclose the All-India Institute 
of Medical Sciences and the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and 
Research (Amendment) Bill. 2007, as passed by Lok S abha at its sitting held 
on the 22nd November. 2007." 
Sir, I lay a copy of the Bill on the Table. 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: The Short Duration Discussion on the proposal to set 
up SEZ in Nandigram, West Bengal, and consequent large-scale violence is 
concluded. 
The House is adjourned to meet at 11.00 A.M. tomorrow. 
The House then adjourned at twelve minutes past 
eight of the clock till eleven of the clock on 
Friday, the 23rd November, 2007.
